title: TCO Heuristics and Rapid Experiments for Hybrid Hosting
summary: Working notes and small-batch experiments to quickly bound TCO differences between on-prem full-stack, cloud VPC-hosted, and hybrid mixes. Focus is on levers we can change in 2-6 weeks (bundle mix, support tiering, HW refresh cadence, quantization profile adoption). Not a final model; a pragmatic checklist + spreadsheet sketch for eng/product to run 3 scenario sweeps.
core_assumptions: 1) Baseline workload is 100 qps sustained equivalent to 3M tokens/day. 2) Latency SLO target: p95 < 250ms; capacity planning accounts for burst factor 1.6. 3) On-prem hardware amortized over 4 years; cloud reserved instance discounts take 36-month commitments where applicable. 4) Licensing: two axes - platform license per GPU (annual) and per-seat support. 5) Efficiency levers (mixed precision, 8-bit quant, batching) reduce compute unit cost by 15-40% depending on model family.
key_levers:
- Hardware mix: A100 vs H100 vs CPU-heavy edge nodes.
- Utilization assumptions: baseline 60% vs 80% (engineering ops).
- Support tier split: standard (email, 24hr), premium (SRE on-call), enterprise (onsite/white-glove).
- Licensing bundling: flat platform fee + per-GPU + per-seat vs all-in-one enterprise license.
- Model strategy: single larger model vs sharded smaller models; effect on kernel utilization and memory.
- Software optimizations: prefix caching, KV reuse, continuous batching settings.
- Refresh cadence: 3yr vs 4yr replacement; effect on depreciation and spare-parts OPEX.
recommended_experiments:
(short-run, measurable)
1) Quantization Pilot: convert a production 7B model to 8-bit and run 2-week A/B traffic split; measure per-token cost delta and latency tail impact.
2) Support-tier Pricing Elasticity: offer 5 pilot customers two different support bundles for 3 months, track churn risk signals and time-to-resolution metrics.
3) Capacity Buffer Reduction: conservative burst factor 1.6 -> 1.3 via autoscaler tuning and warm caches; simulate impact on committed capacity for Dedicated and on-prem spare pool reduction.
4) Hybrid Routing Policy: route low-latency traffic to dedicated cloud region, batchable offline jobs to on-prem; run cost attribution for 30 days and reconcile to model.
5) License Mix Swap: create a hypothetical 20-customer portfolio and compare cost under per-GPU licensing vs enterprise-flat; run sensitivity where 20%-40% customers require enterprise features.
Each experiment should produce: one CSV of daily cost by category, one short 1-page observation note, and an updated scenario row in the TCO spreadsheet.
spreadsheet_template_sample:
Columns (suggested for scenario sweeps): Scenario name | Deployment mode | GPUs | GPU type | Utilization % | Annual HW CapEx | Annual HW Deprec | Annual Opex (power/cooling/staff) | Platform license (annual) | Support fees (annual) | Network egress | Reserved cloud cost (if applicable) | Service misc (backups, DR) | Estimated tokens/day | Cost per 1k tokens | Notes

Quick example row (text): Hybrid-light | hybrid | 16 | H100 | 70 | $1,120,000 | $280,000 | $150,000 | $120,000 | $90,000 | $20,000 | $360,000 | $12,000,000 | $0.0045 | use 8-bit quant in production for LLM-7B
sensitivity_checks:
Minimum sanity checks to include in sheet:
- If utilization < 30% on on-prem, flag: likely better for cloud burst model.
- If network egress > $50k/month, recalc hybrid thresholds (may flip decision).
- If support tier mix > 30% enterprise, enterprise-flat licensing can dominate per-GPU models.
- Break-even horizon: compute years to breakeven under given workload growth (5% and 20% CAGR).
- Run a slim-line scenario that assumes 25% improvement from batching and caching; this shows theoretical lower bound for marginal cost/unit.
operational_checklist:
- Collect last 12 months of token volume and 95/99 latency distributions (from Console).
- Inventory current SAN/NAS and rack PDU capacity for potential on-prem expansion.
- Validate power/cooling rates with facilities (kWh and overhead multiplier).
- Map customers to feature buckets that drive enterprise license needs.
- Run initial quantization pilot in staging on a mirrored dataset with traffic capture.
- Prepare a 2-week cost reconciliation to capture anomalous egress or unexpected license surcharges.
deliverables_and_timeline:
Week 0-2: finalize baseline numbers, set up experiment dashboards.
Week 2-6: run quantization + hybrid routing experiments.
Week 6-8: synthesize results, update TCO sheet with empirical deltas.
Week 8-10: prepare recommendation memo with 2–3 recommended bundles and suggested pricing bands for licensing/support.
Expected artifacts: CSVs from each experiment, updated scenario spreadsheet (one row per scenario), 2-page recommendation memo for GTM/finance.
short_conclusion: This doc is a tactical playbook to get from assumptions to data-driven TCO guidance within ~2 months. The focus is on levers that materially move per-token economics (quantization, utilization, license mix). Next step: assign owners for the three pilots (quantization, support-tier elasticity, hybrid routing) and book a review in 6 weeks.
notes_to_reviewers: Please annotate the sheet template with real numbers where you have them (power rates, discount commitments, current headcount for ops). If you own a pilot, add your name to the collaborators list and note expected sampling window. Known unknowns: real-world support labor effort per enterprise customer and network egress patterns for hybrid flows.
